topic: Aufbau Principle, Pauli Exclusion Principle and Hund's Rule
title: 4s Before 3d? Filling Rules Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A water tank fills from the bottom up, strangers on a bus take empty seats before anyone shares, and no two passengers hold the same seat number. Electrons follow the very same three habits. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 2, Structure of Atom) we learn the three rules that decide how an atom fills its orbitals.

You will see why energy depends on n alone in hydrogen but on n and l in atoms with many electrons, and use the n + l rule to order the subshells (1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s, 3d, 4p, 5s). Then the three rules: the Aufbau principle (fill in order of increasing energy), the Pauli exclusion principle (no two electrons share all four quantum numbers, so at most two per orbital with opposite spins) and Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity (one electron in each p, d or f orbital before pairing, with parallel spins). On the molecule bench we fill nitrogen one electron at a time and watch oxygen start pairing. We sort 4p, 5s and 4d step by step, fill phosphorus (3 unpaired electrons), and finish with the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 24 of our PUC Chemistry series. Episode 23 covers the shapes of s, p and d orbitals.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
